subject: Proof-of-Value: success criteria, owners and risk log
messages:
From: Emily Chen <emily@cloudscale.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Jul 2026 16:08:00 -0700
Subject: Quick follow-up from today's demo + PoV ask

Thanks for the demo earlier — Carlos and I walked through examples and overall it looks promising. We'd like to run a short proof-of-value to validate latency and cost on a representative workload before we commit to Dedicated.

High-level ask from our side:
- 3–4 week PoV starting as early as Jul 20
- Success criteria: 95th pct latency < 450ms for 512-token generation; embedding recall >= 0.82 on our evaluation set; end-to-end cost per 1k queries under $X (we'll share target offline)
- We'll provide a ~10k-row sample dataset and evaluation script by Jul 19

Can you confirm owners, an initial plan, and any immediate risks we should know about? Also please include a short checklist of infra items so our cloud team can prep.

Thanks — Emily
Emily Chen
Head of ML Infrastructure, CloudScale Inc.
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Thu, 15 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up from today's demo + PoV ask

Hi Emily — great to hear the demo landed. Quick recap and proposed next steps (post-call):

Recap / scope
- Goal: 3–4 week proof-of-value to validate latency, cost, and embedding quality on your production-like sample set.
- Target success criteria (proposal):
  • 95th pct generation latency < 450ms (512 tokens)
  • Embedding recall >= 0.82 on your eval set
  • End-to-end infra cost target we can tune against once you share the baseline

Owners and roles
- Redwood lead (technical): Hannah Schmitt — PoV runbook, eval harness, daily triage
- Redwood commercial: Marissa Cole — deal owner, procurement / contracting
- Redwood infra escalation: Lukas Meyer — on-call for infra/regression escalations
- CloudScale lead: Emily Chen — dataset delivery, evaluation acceptance

Kickoff / timeline
- Jul 19: CloudScale delivers sample dataset + evaluation script
- Jul 20: Technical kickoff (30–60m) and environment onboarding
- Jul 20–Aug 10: PoV run window (3 weeks), weekly checkpoints on Tuesdays
- Aug 11: Formal acceptance review and next-steps decision

Immediate risks I want to flag now (initial triage)
- Large tokenized payloads can increase GPU memory pressure — we'll validate with your sample and may request smaller batches or sequence windowing.
- If dataset contains long-context sequences we may need to swap to a model variant with extended context or enable streaming to avoid tail latency spikes.

I'll put together a short runbook and a config stub for your infra team. Marissa — will loop you on procurement cadence and expected contract timeline.

Thanks — Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Emily Chen <emily@cloudscale.com>, Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 17 Jul 2026 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up from today's demo + PoV ask

Thanks — quick technical note after reviewing the sample schema Emily shared offline. I want to call out an immediate blocker risk and proposed mitigations so we can decide before kickoff:

Blocking issue (severity: high):
- The sample includes multi-doc entries that, when tokenized, frequently exceed 8k tokens per item. Our default inference batch and KV cache sizing for the target model will OOM on the smaller GPU shapes we normally provision for PoVs.

Mitigations (short-term / PoV run):
1) Shard long records into windowed slices (we can provide a small utility) — reduces per-request token count
2) Reduce batch size to 1–2 for long-context items and enable streaming responses on generation to avoid allocating full output token buffers
3) For embedding runs, run in incremental chunks with prefix caching disabled for the highest-memory sets
4) If needed, switch to a 32GB GPU profile for the PoV window (Marissa — we'll mark this as a possible add-on cost)

Escalation path if we hit OOMs beyond mitigations:
- Step 1: Dev triages and applies immediate config changes (batch size, windowing)
- Step 2: Lukas to escalate to infra on-call for temporary capacity bump or different instance family
- Step 3: If persistent, schedule a joint deep-dive and pause the PoV until root cause is addressed (we'll keep you informed and protect your PoV window)

Attachments: POV-config.yml (small config stub), dataset-sample.csv (10 rows) — sending as stubs in case your team wants to review locally.

I'll join the Jul 20 kickoff and bring a short troubleshooting playbook.

— Dev
Dev Patel
Principal Infrastructure Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Emily Chen <emily@cloudscale.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up from today's demo + PoV ask

Thanks all — appreciate the clear plan and the early flag on the tokenization issue. We accept the mitigations and will: 
- Deliver the 10k-row sample and evaluation script by EOD Jul 19 (per plan)
- Split long documents where feasible and run the windowing utility you mentioned
- Confirm whether we need the 32GB GPU bump after the first 48 hours of the run

We'd like weekly 30m check-ins on Tuesdays at 9am PT during the PoV window — Marissa, Hannah, Dev, Lukas, and our ML infra lead Carlos included.

Looking forward to kickoff on Jul 20.

Best,
Emily
Emily Chen
Head of ML Infrastructure, CloudScale Inc.
